sections.html:
Paulding is a fast-growing western suburb of metro Atlanta, with Dallas as the county seat and government offices clustered on Constitution Boulevard. The mid-2025 estimate is 190,996 people, up 13.3 percent from 168,630 in the 2020 base, across 312.35 square miles of land.

Half of owner-occupied homes are worth more than $326,300, and 80.8 percent of households own where they live. Median gross rent is $1,772 a month, and 1,326 permits were issued in 2025. A seller in a newer subdivision competes with new construction, which sets buyer expectations for finishes and the age of systems. Workers travel a mean of 39.6 minutes to their jobs, so many residents commute toward Atlanta.

On the tax side, value is fixed on January 1, taxed at 40 percent of that figure, and the commissioner multiplies the result by the millage. The sections below cover the points that come up when a Paulding County house is sold.

The assessors and the tax commissioner divide the job, and deeds sit with a third office. The Board of Assessors sets values, takes homestead applications and hears the first level of appeals. The tax commissioner bills and collects. The Clerk of Superior Court, in the courthouse, keeps recorded deeds.

Paulding tax offices in Dallas
OfficeLocationPhoneHours
Tax Commissioner240 Constitution Boulevard, Room 3006, Dallas, GA 30132(770) 443-7581Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.
Board of Assessors240 Constitution Boulevard, Room 3082, Dallas, GA 30132770-443-7606Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

The phone line may be cut off early so the commissioner's office can close at 4:00 p.m. The assessors accept homestead applications by email, and the board's public meetings run on Wednesdays at 10 a.m. in the third-floor conference room.

Property tax is due November 15 every year. Go by the date printed on your bill when you plan a payoff or a closing.

After the deadline, charges stack up this way:

  • Interest posts to the account on the 16th of every month, calculated as prime plus 3 percent spread over twelve months.
  • A FIFA, which is the county's lien filing, is recorded at the Clerk of Superior Court's office thirty days after the delinquent notice date, and credit bureaus can read it there.
  • Penalties of 5 percent land at the 120-day mark and recur on that cycle until they reach 20 percent in total.
  • Accounts that stay unpaid are turned over to a contractor, and administrative and levy fees of $215 or more can be added to prepare the parcel for tax sale.

A mobile home follows its own calendar. Mobile home bills normally mail near January 2, fall due April 1 and pick up a 10 percent penalty the next day.

You have 45 days, which is about six and a half weeks, counted from the mailing of the notice. A late filing cannot be accepted, so mark the envelope date when the notice arrives. Grounds are limited to whether the parcel is taxable, what it is worth and whether that value is fair next to similar homes. Anger about the millage or the total on the bill will not carry an appeal.

The path runs in a fixed order:

  • Send the appeal to the Board of Assessors first, which re-checks its number and replies with a decision.
  • No deal at that stage means a hearing before the Board of Equalization.
  • Arbitration is the alternative to that board, and the assessors' staff can walk you through it.
  • If you are still unhappy after that decision, the next step is Superior Court.

The assessors keep an appeals page with a form and a guide to reading the notice, plus a list of recent sales used for comparison. Someone serving abroad can have a relative or friend file for them, with 90 days instead of 45. Mobile home owners have the same 45 days to declare a different value.

Exemptions are never granted automatically, so apply with the Board of Assessors. Expect to show residency and citizenship papers, such as a Georgia license or ID card, and your name has to be on the deed. You can claim a homestead on only one property, including property in other counties or states.

Beyond the standard exemption, the county lists these categories:

  • Lower school tax for owners aged 65 or more.
  • Relief for owners with a total and permanent disability.
  • A break for a veteran rated fully disabled from service.
  • A full homestead break for the unmarried survivor of a peace officer or firefighter killed on duty.
  • An added exemption for homes inside the city limits of Hiram, approved by that city's voters in 2017.

Eligibility turns on owning and occupying the home on January 1. Applications must arrive by April 1, so file as early as you can. A change in ownership, marriage, divorce or death requires a fresh application with the supporting paperwork. Farmland and timber programs come with a covenant that runs at least 10 years, so a seller of acreage should read the agreement before listing.

sections.h2: What happens to the tax when a house sells?
sections.html:
Your purchase agreement spells out how the year's bill is shared with the buyer, and the settlement statement shows the result.

Request a balance figure from the commissioner before the sign goes up, including any interest, penalty or lien recorded against the parcel. A balance still open comes out of your proceeds, which hands the buyer a parcel with nothing owing. If the sale happens after a November due date but before the bill is paid, confirm in writing who pays it.

After closing, the new owner should make a fresh homestead application, because a change in ownership ends the old one. The seller can notify the assessors that the exemption no longer applies. The courthouse deed room can supply a copy of your recorded deed, which the buyer's title work will want.

If the account has gone delinquent, work out the order of events. Interest posts on the 16th of each month, the lien filing follows thirty days after the delinquent notice date, and the 5 percent penalties arrive at 120 days. Paying before the lien is recorded keeps your credit record clean and spares the buyer's title company a cleanup.

If a FIFA is already on the record, you can still sell. The closing agent pays the tax, interest, penalties and fees from your proceeds, then records the release. Ask the commissioner for a payoff good through the closing date, since interest changes on the 16th.

A cash sale can shorten this process because there is no lender waiting on a clear tax record. The amount owed is still deducted from what you receive at the table, so the earlier you know the figure, the fewer surprises at closing.

faqs.q: What is the property tax due date in Paulding County?
faqs.a: November 15 each year. Go by the bill in your hands when you plan a closing.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Paulding County property value?
faqs.a: Call the Board of Assessors at 770-443-7606. The tax commissioner at (770) 443-7581 handles billing, payments and payoff figures, not values.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal in Paulding County?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the notice mailing. The county states that appeals cannot be filed after that period ends.

faqs.q: Does a Paulding County homestead exemption renew by itself?
faqs.a: Yes. After approval it carries over from year to year until the owner moves, the title changes or a different exemption is sought. A buyer starts a new application after closing.

faqs.q: What does Paulding County charge on late property tax?
faqs.a: Interest is charged monthly, and a penalty layer stacks on after four months. Its ceiling is one fifth of the tax, so a long-ignored bill grows quickly.
